result:
Both integrate changes from one branch into another. Difference is history shape.

**`git merge`**: joins two branches with a new merge commit (two parents). Existing commits unchanged. History non-linear but true to what happened. Safe on shared branches.

**`git rebase`**: replays your commits on top of the target branch. Creates new commits with new SHAs. History linear, no merge commit. Rewrites history.

```
Before:        A---B---C  main
                    \
                     D---E  feature

merge:         A---B---C---M  main
                    \     /
                     D---E

rebase:        A---B---C---D'---E'  feature
```

Conflicts: merge resolves once. Rebase may ask per replayed commit.

Never rebase commits others already pulled: their history diverges from yours, and you need a force push to publish. Rebase local, unpushed work only.

Common use: rebase feature branch onto `main` to update it, then merge into `main`.
